subject: Coffee & Tea
title: What Happens During Roasting
description: Learn What Happens During Roasting in one minute.

hook.text: Green coffee beans have no coffee flavor. Roasting triggers over 1,000 chemical reactions that create it.

buildup.text: Beans enter the roaster at 200°C. Moisture evaporates, then sugars and amino acids start reacting.

discovery.text: The Maillard reaction—same as searing a steak—creates hundreds of flavor and aroma compounds.

twist.text: Caramelization happens separately, breaking sugars into sweet, nutty, and bitter molecules all at once.

climax.text: A roaster's job is controlling time and temperature to balance these reactions for the desired flavor.

punchline.text: Green, tasteless seeds become complex flavor bombs. Heat does it all.

quiz.question: What reaction is primarily responsible for coffee's roasted flavors?

details.summary: Roasting transforms green coffee beans through hundreds of chemical reactions. Sugars caramelize, amino acids undergo Maillard reactions, and gases build until the bean cracks. The roaster controls time and temperature to develop sweetness, acidity, and body in balance.
details.whyItMatters: Roasting is where flavor is created from raw potential. A great bean poorly roasted tastes flat, while skilled roasting reveals complexity hidden in the green seed.
takeaways: Maillard reactions create most of coffee's complex flavors
First crack signals the start of drinkable roast levels
Time and temperature curves determine the flavor outcome

faq.question: What chemical reactions occur during roasting?
faq.answer: The Maillard reaction between sugars and amino acids creates hundreds of aromatic compounds. Caramelization breaks down sugars into sweet and bitter flavors. Strecker degradation produces key aroma molecules. Over 800 volatile compounds have been identified in roasted coffee.

faq.question: What temperature does coffee roast at?
faq.answer: Green beans enter the roaster around room temperature and reach 196 degrees Celsius at first crack. Light roasts stop shortly after, medium roasts continue to about 210 degrees, and dark roasts push past 225 degrees toward second crack.
